problems.explain: 70 points is 1 SD below. Each band of one SD on one side holds 34%, 13.5%, 2.35% and 0.15% going out from the mean, so this is 34 + 34 + 13.5 + 2.35 + 0.15 = 84%. (68%, 95% and 99.7% each count both sides of the mean; one side alone is half.) So about 84%.

prompt.v: The scores on a test are normally distributed, with a mean of 80 points and a standard deviation of 5 points. About what percent are above 95 points?

problems.text: normal percent: mean 80 sd 5, from 95 to inf
problems.explain: 95 points is 3 SD above. Each band of one SD on one side holds 34%, 13.5%, 2.35% and 0.15% going out from the mean, so this is 0.15%. (68%, 95% and 99.7% each count both sides of the mean; one side alone is half.) So about 0.15%.

prompt.v: The scores on a test are normally distributed, with a mean of 80 points and a standard deviation of 7 points. About what percent are below 80 points?

problems.text: normal percent: mean 80 sd 7, from -inf to 80
problems.explain: 80 points is the mean. Each band of one SD on one side holds 34%, 13.5%, 2.35% and 0.15% going out from the mean, so this is 0.15 + 2.35 + 13.5 + 34 = 50%. (68%, 95% and 99.7% each count both sides of the mean; one side alone is half.) So about 50%.

prompt.v: These are 6 daily high temperatures, in °C: 10, 12, 10, 18, 24, 28. Find the standard deviation, dividing by the number of values.

problems.explain: The mean is 10 + 12 + 10 + 18 + 24 + 28 = 102, ÷ 6 = 17. The distances from it, squared, are 49, 25, 49, 1, 49, 121, which add to 294. Divide by 6: 294 ÷ 6 = 49, and take the square root: √49 = 7. (Without the square root, 49 is the variance, in squared units.) So 7°C.
